title: An Off-Cycle Raise That the New Approval Rule Reclaimed
scenario_text:
A people-ops partner at Ashgrove Robotics must decide whether a manager can approve a 12% off-cycle raise, given how a comparable raise was handled last year.

**Decision A (2023-10-04)**
A manager approved a 12% off-cycle raise for an engineer to counter an outside offer. Note: 'Under the compensation policy then in effect, managers could approve off-cycle raises up to 15% at their own discretion.'

**Current request C (2024-11-06)**
The same manager wants to approve a 12% off-cycle raise for a different engineer, again citing retention risk. The manager has asked People Ops to process it 'the same way as last year.'

**Compensation Policy (current, updated 2024-07-01, in force now)**
Off-cycle raises up to 8% may be approved by the direct manager. Off-cycle raises above 8% require BOTH VP approval and Compensation Committee review, regardless of the retention justification. The prior manager-discretion ceiling of 15% was removed in the July 2024 update.

**Slack — #people-ops**
Manager: 'I approved a 12% off-cycle raise myself last October and it went through fine. Let's run this one the same way — same size, same reason.'
Partner: 'Last October was under the old comp policy. The manager-discretion ceiling changed in July — a 12% raise isn't something you can sign off alone anymore.'

There is no dispute that the retention risk is genuine; the question is who may approve a raise of this size now.
question: How should the People Ops partner handle the manager's 12% off-cycle raise request?
choices: Let the manager approve the 12% raise at their own discretion, consistent with the October 2023 raise of the same size.
Route the 12% raise for VP approval and Compensation Committee review, because the July 2024 policy removed the manager-discretion ceiling and now requires both for any raise above 8%.
Approve the raise at 8% under manager discretion and treat the remaining 4% as denied.
Deny the raise outright, since off-cycle raises above 8% are no longer permitted.
